currentContext.expansion: UltraTech's expansion story is one of combined organic and inorganic capacity addition. What began with a single cement plant commissioned by the Aditya Birla Group in the mid-1980s has become, in the Company's description, the world's largest cement company by sales volume and capacity excluding China. Since December 2020 the Company has undertaken multiple phases of expansion, complemented by targeted debottlenecking initiatives across locations that further enhanced production capability, with the added footprint strengthening pan-India presence particularly in the Northern markets. During FY 2025-26 the Company expanded cement capacities by 8 MTPA and completed the integration of the India Cements and Kesoram Industries cement assets representing 26.3 MTPA of cumulative installed capacity; 100% migration of those assets to the UltraTech brand was completed in March 2026 and cost and efficiency improvement is underway. India grey cement installed capacity stood at 191.36 MTPA at end-FY 2025-26 versus 183.36 MTPA a year earlier (a 4% increase), with cement production in FY26 higher by 13% at 143.83 million tonnes and capacity utilisation at 77% compared with 78%. On 17th April, 2026 the Company crossed the landmark 200 MTPA installed capacity milestone, taking total grey cement capacity including overseas operations to 205.5 MTPA. Looking forward, management has committed to invest Rs 16,000 crore to add a further 37 MTPA and reach a total grey cement capacity of 242.5 MTPA by FY 2027-28. The manufacturing and distribution footprint as at 31st March, 2026 comprised integrated units, grinding units, bulk terminals, a jetty and white cement/putty units across North, West, East, Central and South India, alongside overseas capacity of 4.4 MTPA in the UAE (3 grinding units and 1 clinkerisation unit), 1.0 MTPA in Bahrain (1 grinding unit) and a 1.5 MTPA bulk terminal in Sri Lanka. Downstream footprint includes 465 ready-mix concrete units and over 5,500 UltraTech Building Solutions outlets, supporting the shift to an integrated building-solutions provider. The Company positions this build-out against an Indian market where installed cement capacity stood at 718 million tonnes per annum at the close of FY26 and independent agencies estimate 100 million tonnes of new grinding capacity will be commissioned over the two years ending FY28.

risks.risk: GHG emissions and carbon-intensity exposure (carbon-intensive sector, carbon tax)
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications: in cement manufacturing limestone is the major material and fuel is required for heating, so CO2 is released from calcination of limestone and combustion of fuel; the Company states GHG emissions may impact business continuity and cause business disruption. Mitigation is SBTi-validated voluntary targets (27% Scope 1 and 69% Scope 2 reduction by 2032 off a 2017 base), an enhanced circular economy, 100% energy transition, a new product portfolio, and piloting CCU technologies through the GCCA consortium.

risks.risk: Health and safety of employees, workers and contractor workforce
risks.note: Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications; the Company says it places great importance on health and safety and endeavours to make the workplace safe for all employees, thereby enhancing wellbeing and productivity. Mitigation is a 'Zero harm culture' with initiatives such as 'Pratibimb' (cluster-head walk-through inspections across units), contractor connect programmes ('Hamein apki parva hain'), investigation, digitalisation and corrective/preventive actions. Exposure is amplified by a very large non-permanent workforce (58,764 other-than-permanent workers of 64,869 total workers).

risks.risk: Energy and fuel cost volatility - crude and petroleum coke prices
risks.note: Management names the trajectory of crude and petroleum coke prices, given the continuing situation in West Asia, as the first of three external factors meriting close monitoring through the year; it will determine the pace of pricing actions across regions. Elevated international crude prices are also listed among India's notable headwinds.

risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption - West Asia conflict and the Strait of Hormuz
risks.note: The Board's report lists protraction of the West Asia conflict and possible disruption of energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz among the principal downside risks to the global outlook, with an IMF adverse scenario placing world growth as low as 2.5% should the conflict escalate further. This transmits into input costs and supply chains for a fuel-intensive manufacturer.

Management flags the actual realisation of the South-West Monsoon against the India Meteorological Department's below-normal projection as a factor that will influence rural demand in the second half of the year; the prospect of a sub-normal monsoon is separately listed among the economy's headwinds, partly cushioned by PMAY-G, MGNREGA and MSP supports.

risks.risk: Tariff policy and currency - US tariff policy and rupee weakness
risks.note: The third external factor management says merits monitoring: the evolution of United States tariff policy and consequent pressure on the rupee will shape the external-sector backdrop and the affordability of imported inputs. A record-low rupee and tariff-related pressures on the external sector are listed among domestic headwinds.

risks.risk: Industry supply addition and utilisation pressure
risks.note: Installed cement production capacity in India stood at 718 million tonnes per annum at the close of FY26, and independent agencies estimate 100 million tonnes of new grinding capacity will be commissioned over the two years ending FY28 - supply growth against demand estimates of 6 to 7.5% for FY27. The Company's own India capacity utilisation was 77% in FY26 versus 78% in FY25 even as capacity rose 4%.

Manufacturing accounts for ~95% of turnover and cement and clinker alone ~92%, with exports contributing only 0.25% of total turnover - so earnings are almost entirely levered to Indian cement demand, cement pricing and Indian construction cycles, with negligible export diversification.

one-line thesis: Highest-ever Q1 across volume, revenue, EBITDA and PAT: domestic grey-cement volume +13.1% (well ahead of an estimated 7-8% industry), 81% utilization on a 200 MT base, EBITDA Rs 5,146 cr (+12%, first Rs 5,000 cr+ April-June), PAT Rs 2,604 cr (+17.2%) — all while absorbing the sharpest imported-fuel shock in memory (West Asia war, Strait of Hormuz, crude >$100) and holding operating EBITDA/ton steady above Rs 1,200. The India Cements turnaround is compounding visibly (EBITDA/ton Rs 386→603 over three quarters; brand migration 100% done; Rs 1,000/ton "in sight" by Q4FY28), the growth runway to 242 MT+ is funded and under construction (Rs 17,000 cr, secured limestone), net debt/EBITDA improved to 0.87x, and the new Cables & Wires business reaffirms a Q3FY27 launch. The one near-term caveat: Q2FY27 will look optically soft (monsoon + full war-cost flow-through = ~Rs 130-140/ton sequential cost rise), but management frames it as usual seasonality, not a trend change. The whole equity story is brand + premiumization in a retail (individual-homebuilder) market.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > Reported ICL revenue Rs 1,013 cr vs Rs 1,021 cr LY looks flat, but that's an accounting change (ex-factory reporting from Q1'27); on a like-for-like ex-freight basis it's Rs 993 cr vs Rs 821 cr = +21% revenue / +19% volume. Q1 one-off cost inflation ≈ Rs 40 fuel + Rs 20 bags.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Volume: double-digit growth targeted for FY27 ("Yes, we are targeting double-digit volume growth this year").

Capacity: grey cement 212.7 MT by end-FY27; consolidated beyond 242 MT in 2-2.5 yrs (Rs 17,000 cr capex, secured limestone); India ~235 MT by Mar-2028 (37 MT added across FY27-28). Beyond 240 MT — plans being drawn; inorganic if opportunities arise.

India Cements EBITDA Rs 1,000/ton "very much in sight", full capex benefit flowing from Q4FY28; ICL green power ~3% → ~86% of power by end-FY28; ICL merger into standalone ~Q4FY28 (or a quarter earlier).

Cables & Wires: commissioning + product launch Q3FY27 (Oct-Dec 2026), on-schedule/on-budget; Rs 1,800 cr program (Rs 888 cr spent/committed). No further C&W capex planned (mature-and-milk). No revenue guidance ("sky is the limit… profitable, grounded, grow with market").
Consolidated EBITDA/ton Rs 1,400 target: Jan-Mar 2028 quarter (Q4FY28), "without any war."
Q2FY27: ~Rs 130-140/ton sequential cost increase (fuel + maintenance + operating deleverage, all-in) → optically softer quarter; industry Q1 volume est. ~7-8%.
Capital allocation: all OCF ploughed into cement growth + dividends (dividend as % of profits); "expecting good dividends."
order book & pipeline: No order book (commodity manufacturer); demand read via macro pipeline management cited as "tomorrow's cement demand": Maharashtra Rs 20,000 cr shipbuilding cluster (Mazagaon Dock); Odisha Ganjam deep seaport + Paradip shipbuilding (Rs 50,000 cr+); Tamil Nadu ~Rs 18,000 cr data-centre + shipbuilding MoU; Ahmedabad-Dholera semi-HSR (Rs 20,000 cr+); metros (Ahmedabad/Bangalore/Mumbai/Pune/UP); Rs 30,000 cr NIIF infusion; Vadhavan port (packages awarded); Ken-Betwa river-linking. Housing/urban real estate (~55-60% of cement demand) strong: Mumbai registrations +6%, top-8 cities unit sales up, Mumbai SRA 850-acre redevelopment. Network: 76 operating facilities, ~2,000 warehouses, 150,000 channel partners, 477 RMC plants, 5,000+ UBS stores, ~16,000 employees.
segment / subsidiary detail: UltraTech core grey cement: +13.1% volume, 81% utilization; regional Q1 growth — East slowest (elections/labour), South & North just below 15%, West & Central above 15%. East a multi-year (2-4 yr) up-cycle (land reforms, elections).

India Cements (ICL): turnaround "no longer a promise" — EBITDA/ton Rs 386 (Q2FY26) → Rs 400 → Rs 509 → Rs 603 (Q1FY27); +21% rev/+19% vol (LFL); brand migration 100%; Rs 2,000 cr cost-improvement capex (WHR/preheater/cooler); green power 3%→86% by FY28; conversion ratio 1.5x; Rs 1,000/ton in sight (Q4FY28); merger ~Q4FY28.
Kesoram: brand converted to UltraTech (was B/C category).
RMC: 477 plants (largest in India) but only ~3.5% of UltraTech's sales — a surrogate/service, not the demand driver (India still a retail/branded market).

Cables & Wires (new): facility complete, trials on, regulatory approvals in place, channel onboarding at pace; launch Q3FY27; aluminium sourced from Hindalco (4-hr lead); WC high initially, →~30 days by Apr-Jun'27.
growth verticals / optionality: Capacity to 242 MT+ (funded, under construction, secured limestone) + "beyond 240" plans being drawn (organic + inorganic optionality).
India Cements margin convergence to standalone UltraTech (Rs 1,000/ton, Q4FY28) — a large embedded earnings lever.
Cables & Wires — new building-materials adjacency leveraging brand/distribution.
Green power to 2.5-3 GW — structural cost advantage (already 47% of power, cheaper).
Premiumization + blended-cement trade mix — compounding blended realizations "regardless of headline price."
Urbanization runway: India 35% urban → 39% by 2030 (vs Indonesia 59%); 63 → 71 million-plus cities by 2030.
6a. moat & competitive position: Brand + distribution scale unmatched: 76 facilities, ~150,000 channel partners, 5,000+ UBS dedicated outlets, ~50%+ dedicated transporters, 477 RMC plants — "nobody else can come close."

Premium pricing power in a retail market: India is an individual-homebuilder (retail) market where cement, like TMT/paints, is branded; customers "don't shop for the cheapest bag" → durable premium. Evidenced by converting B/C-category ICL/Kesoram buyers to premium UltraTech without losing that market share (+21.3% brand growth).

Cost-curve resilience: absorbed the fuel shock better than any peer via 47% green power, AFR substitution, 360 km lead distance, 1.5x clinker conversion, and inventory buffers ("we absorbed the shock better than any peer, and we will harvest the relief faster").
Secured limestone across the entire committed expansion — no raw-material constraint on growth.
Multi-year volume/EBITDA outperformance vs industry (e.g., Dec'25 +15% vs industry ~half; Mar'26 +9% vs <half; Jun'26 +13%).
margins & cost dynamics: Held operating EBITDA/ton >Rs 1,200 despite: fuel Rs 874→915 (+5%), packing bags Rs 9→12 (~Rs 20/ton), industrial diesel +~50% (Rs 78-80 → Rs 150s → lifting limestone-raising cost). Pet coke now costlier than coal in energy terms → shifting to domestic coal.
Q2FY27: ~Rs 130-140/ton sequential cost rise (fuel/maintenance/deleverage) — management insists it's normal monsoon-quarter seasonality, partly offset by scale (larger volume base).
Structural levers: green power 47%→2.5-3 GW; lead distance 367→360 km; power consumption/rate down; AFR ramp. Full cost-saving number to be given annually (not quarterly).

Prices: all-India exit prices improved through June (East/South led, Central/West steady, North consistent); industry expected to hold prices through monsoon on cost pass-through. "Prices move with demand… if cost curve comes down, not necessary prices reduce."
capex / expansion (watch slippage): FY26 capex ~Rs 9,500 cr deployed. Q1FY27: 8.7 MT commissioned (Shahjahanpur, Visakhapatnam, Patratu) → 200.1 MT domestic / 205.5 MT total.
Under execution: Rs 17,000 cr over 2-2.5 yrs → grey 212.7 MT (end-FY27), consolidated 242 MT+, India 235 MT by Mar-2028 (37 MT FY27-28). All internal-accrual funded, secured limestone.
Cables & Wires Rs 1,800 cr (Rs 888 cr committed) — launch Q3FY27, on-budget.
Watch: Q2 seasonal softness (monsoon + kiln maintenance), war-driven fuel/freight, ICL capex pace (Rs 2,000 cr) toward the Q4FY28 Rs 1,000/ton milestone.
capital allocation: "Fully booked" cash flows → all OCF into growth + dividends. No further C&W investment planned near-term ("mature and milk"). Dividend policy = % of profits (Board view); prior year had a special component; "expecting good dividends."
Net debt/EBITDA 0.94x → 0.87x, guided <1x FY27. Growth + cost-improvement capex all internally funded.
ICL: capex completion + non-core land disposal + operating-parameter alignment before standalone merger (~Q4FY28).
risks & watch-items: West Asia war / fuel & freight: crude >$100, coal/pet-coke elevated, ocean-freight insurance up to 4-5% (from <1%); "I don't know when it will end." Q2 full flow-through.
Q2FY27 optical softness: monsoon + maintenance + war costs (~Rs 130-140/ton sequential) — management asks to "look through the noise."
Monsoon/weather divergence: dry pockets (Rajasthan) → next-year rural demand risk; most states have had rain (watch Aug-Sep).
Near-term macro data points: coal-sector growth slowdown (May), aggregate state capex +2% (Apr-May) — management calls these "timing, not trend."
Demand is the only real risk: CFO — "as long as demand is there, everything else is immaterial"; the flip risk is a structural housing/industrialization/data-centre slowdown (viewed as unlikely).
Cables & Wires execution: new business, initial high working capital, entering a competitive market.
management quality / tone: CFO Atul Daga sole voice — highly confident, "challenger not incumbent" framing, candid on near-term data softness and Q2 cost drag (won't sandbag), precise on cost bridges (fuel Rs 874→915, bags, diesel +50%, coal Rs 1.9→2/Kcal). Heavy emphasis on "we deliver what we commit" — cites delivering 200 MT a year early, brand migration a quarter early, and reaffirming C&W Q3FY27. The one near-term caveat: Q2FY27 will look optically soft (monsoon + full war-cost flow-through = ~Rs 130-140/ton sequential cost rise), but management frames it as usual seasonality, not a trend change. The whole equity story is brand + premiumization in a retail (individual-homebuilder) market.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > Reported ICL revenue Rs 1,013 cr vs Rs 1,021 cr LY looks flat, but that's an accounting change (ex-factory reporting from Q1'27); on a like-for-like ex-freight basis it's Rs 993 cr vs Rs 821 cr = +21% revenue / +19% volume. Q1 one-off cost inflation ≈ Rs 40 fuel + Rs 20 bags.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Volume: double-digit growth targeted for FY27 ("Yes, we are targeting double-digit volume growth this year").

Capacity: grey cement 212.7 MT by end-FY27; consolidated beyond 242 MT in 2-2.5 yrs (Rs 17,000 cr capex, secured limestone); India ~235 MT by Mar-2028 (37 MT added across FY27-28). Beyond 240 MT — plans being drawn; inorganic if opportunities arise.

India Cements EBITDA Rs 1,000/ton "very much in sight", full capex benefit flowing from Q4FY28; ICL green power ~3% → ~86% of power by end-FY28; ICL merger into standalone ~Q4FY28 (or a quarter earlier).

Cables & Wires: commissioning + product launch Q3FY27 (Oct-Dec 2026), on-schedule/on-budget; Rs 1,800 cr program (Rs 888 cr spent/committed). No further C&W capex planned (mature-and-milk). No revenue guidance ("sky is the limit… profitable, grounded, grow with market").
Consolidated EBITDA/ton Rs 1,400 target: Jan-Mar 2028 quarter (Q4FY28), "without any war."
Q2FY27: ~Rs 130-140/ton sequential cost increase (fuel + maintenance + operating deleverage, all-in) → optically softer quarter; industry Q1 volume est. ~7-8%.

order book & pipeline: No order book (commodity manufacturer); demand read via macro pipeline management cited as "tomorrow's cement demand": Maharashtra Rs 20,000 cr shipbuilding cluster (Mazagaon Dock); Odisha Ganjam deep seaport + Paradip shipbuilding (Rs 50,000 cr+); Tamil Nadu ~Rs 18,000 cr data-centre + shipbuilding MoU; Ahmedabad-Dholera semi-HSR (Rs 20,000 cr+); metros (Ahmedabad/Bangalore/Mumbai/Pune/UP); Rs 30,000 cr NIIF infusion; Vadhavan port (packages awarded); Ken-Betwa river-linking. segment / subsidiary detail: UltraTech core grey cement: +13.1% volume, 81% utilization; regional Q1 growth — East slowest (elections/labour), South & North just below 15%, West & Central above 15%. East a multi-year (2-4 yr) up-cycle (land reforms, elections).

India Cements (ICL): turnaround "no longer a promise" — EBITDA/ton Rs 386 (Q2FY26) → Rs 400 → Rs 509 → Rs 603 (Q1FY27); +21% rev/+19% vol (LFL); brand migration 100%; Rs 2,000 cr cost-improvement capex (WHR/preheater/cooler); green power 3%→86% by FY28; conversion ratio 1.5x; Rs 1,000/ton in sight (Q4FY28); merger ~Q4FY28.
Kesoram: brand converted to UltraTech (was B/C category).
RMC: 477 plants (largest in India) but only ~3.5% of UltraTech's sales — a surrogate/service, not the demand driver (India still a retail/branded market).

Cables & Wires (new): facility complete, trials on, regulatory approvals in place, channel onboarding at pace; launch Q3FY27; aluminium sourced from Hindalco (4-hr lead); WC high initially, →~30 days by Apr-Jun'27.
growth verticals / optionality: Capacity to 242 MT+ (funded, under construction, secured limestone) + "beyond 240" plans being drawn (organic + inorganic optionality).
India Cements margin convergence to standalone UltraTech (Rs 1,000/ton, Q4FY28) — a large embedded earnings lever.
Cables & Wires — new building-materials adjacency leveraging brand/distribution.
Green power to 2.5-3 GW — structural cost advantage (already 47% of power, cheaper).
Premiumization + blended-cement trade mix — compounding blended realizations "regardless of headline price."
Urbanization runway: India 35% urban → 39% by 2030 (vs Indonesia 59%); 63 → 71 million-plus cities by 2030.
6a. moat & competitive position: Brand + distribution scale unmatched: 76 facilities, ~150,000 channel partners, 5,000+ UBS dedicated outlets, ~50%+ dedicated transporters, 477 RMC plants — "nobody else can come close."

Premium pricing power in a retail market: India is an individual-homebuilder (retail) market where cement, like TMT/paints, is branded; customers "don't shop for the cheapest bag" → durable premium. Evidenced by converting B/C-category ICL/Kesoram buyers to premium UltraTech without losing that market share (+21.3% brand growth).

Multi-year volume/EBITDA outperformance vs industry (e.g., Dec'25 +15% vs industry ~half; Mar'26 +9% vs <half; Jun'26 +13%).
margins & cost dynamics: Held operating EBITDA/ton >Rs 1,200 despite: fuel Rs 874→915 (+5%), packing bags Rs 9→12 (~Rs 20/ton), industrial diesel +~50% (Rs 78-80 → Rs 150s → lifting limestone-raising cost). Pet coke now costlier than coal in energy terms → shifting to domestic coal.

themes.title: Cement demand & pricing recovery
themes.need: Q1FY27 turned cement from a pricing story into a volume-share-plus-fuel-cost story. ULTRACEMCO grew domestic grey volume +13.1% YoY against an estimated ~7-8% industry, delivered its first Rs 5,000cr+ April-June EBITDA (Rs 5,146cr) with EBITDA/ton held above Rs 1,200, and crossed 200.1 MT domestic capacity a year early - but guided Q2FY27 cost UP ~Rs 130-140/ton and pinned the Rs 1,400/ton consolidated target to Q4FY28. The fuel shock, not price, is the swing factor: JKCEMENT's EBITDA/ton fell to Rs 982 from Rs 1,229 YoY despite +19% grey volume, DALBHARAT flagged pet coke 'surged to nearly $160/t' versus a pre-war $110-115, and NUVOCO defended INR 1,079/ton EBITDA only by cutting petcoke from 37% to 27% of fuel mix in a single quarter. Consolidation is visibly compounding (INDIACEM EBITDA/ton Rs 386->400->509->603 across four quarters; DALBHARAT closed Jaypee at Rs 2,850cr EV with Chunar operational and Rewa on trial within 50 days) even as DALBHARAT slipped its 75mt milestone from FY27 to FY28. SHREECEM/RAMCOCEM/JKLAKSHMI/JSWCEMENT/STARCEMENT/BIRLACORPN ride the same volume + consolidation axis.
themes.driver: Q2FY27 is the guided cost trough - ULTRACEMCO ~Rs 130-140/ton, JKCEMENT ~Rs 150/ton and BIRLACORPN Rs 70-80/ton of incremental cost; then fuel-mix agility (NUVOCO's petcoke swing) and whether DALBHARAT's ~Rs 150/t of procurement savings is really 'permanent, not timing'.

hero.oneLiner: UltraTech Cement is India's largest manufacturer of grey cement, ready-mix concrete and white cement, and — on crossing 200 MTPA installed capacity on 17th April, 2026 — the world's largest cement company by sales volume and capacity excluding China.
